audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for priestly holy-food boundaries, temporary impurity, household eligibility, hired worker/sojourner distinctions, acceptable offerings, animal defects, mother-and-young rule, thanksgiving timing, and sanctification refrain.

verses.restored: YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

familiar.text: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,

modern.text: Then the LORD said to Moses,

original.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר

verses.restored: Speak to Aaron and to his sons, that they keep separate from holy things of children of Israel, and not profane my holy name in what they sanctify to me. I am YHWH.

familiar.text: Speak unto Aaron and to his sons, that they separate themselves from the holy things of the children of Israel, and that they profane not my holy name in those things which they hallow unto me: I am the LORD.

modern.text: “Tell Aaron and his sons to treat with respect the sacred offerings that the Israelites have consecrated to Me, so that they do not profane My holy name. I am the LORD.

original.text: דַּבֵּ֨ר אֶֽל אַהֲרֹ֜ן וְאֶל בָּנָ֗יו וְיִנָּֽזְרוּ֙ מִקָּדְשֵׁ֣י בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְלֹ֥א יְחַלְּל֖וּ אֶת שֵׁ֣ם קָדְשִׁ֑י אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵ֧ם מַקְדִּשִׁ֛ים לִ֖י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Say to them: Throughout your generations, any man from all your seed who draws near to holy things that children of Israel sanctify to YHWH, while his uncleanness is upon him, that soul/life shall be cut off from before me. I am YHWH.

familiar.text: Say unto them, Whosoever he be of all your seed among your generations, that goeth unto the holy things, which the children of Israel hallow unto the LORD, having his uncleanness upon him, that soul shall be cut off from my presence: I am the LORD.

modern.text: Tell them that for the generations to come, if any of their descendants in a state of uncleanness approaches the sacred offerings that the Israelites consecrate to the LORD, that person must be cut off from My presence. I am the LORD.

original.text: אֱמֹ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם לְדֹרֹ֨תֵיכֶ֜ם כָּל אִ֣ישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִקְרַ֣ב מִכָּל זַרְעֲכֶ֗ם אֶל הַקֳּדָשִׁים֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַקְדִּ֤ישׁוּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וְטֻמְאָת֖וֹ עָלָ֑יו וְנִכְרְתָ֞ה הַנֶּ֧פֶשׁ הַהִ֛וא מִלְּפָנַ֖י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Any man from seed of Aaron who is afflicted with scale-disease or has discharge shall not eat from holy things until he is clean. Whoever touches any unclean by dead soul/life, or man from whom emission of seed goes out,

familiar.text: What man soever of the seed of Aaron is a leper, or hath a running issue; he shall not eat of the holy things, until he be clean. And whoso toucheth any thing that is unclean by the dead, or a man whose seed goeth from him;

modern.text: If a descendant of Aaron has a skin disease or a discharge, he may not eat the sacred offerings until he is clean. Whoever touches anything defiled by a corpse or by a man who has an emission of semen,

original.text: אִ֣ישׁ אִ֞ישׁ מִזֶּ֣רַע אַהֲרֹ֗ן וְה֤וּא צָר֨וּעַ֙ א֣וֹ זָ֔ב בַּקֳּדָשִׁים֙ לֹ֣א יֹאכַ֔ל עַ֖ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִטְהָ֑ר וְהַנֹּגֵ֨עַ֙ בְּכָל טְמֵא נֶ֔פֶשׁ א֣וֹ אִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁר תֵּצֵ֥א מִמֶּ֖נּוּ שִׁכְבַת זָֽרַע

verses.restored: or man who touches any swarming thing by which he becomes unclean, or human by whom he becomes unclean, whatever his uncleanness,

familiar.text: Or whosoever toucheth any creeping thing, whereby he may be made unclean, or a man of whom he may take uncleanness, whatsoever uncleanness he hath;

modern.text: or whoever touches a crawling creature or a person that makes him unclean, whatever the uncleanness may be—

original.text: אוֹ אִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִגַּ֔ע בְּכָל שֶׁ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִטְמָא ל֑וֹ א֤וֹ בְאָדָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִטְמָא ל֔וֹ לְכֹ֖ל טֻמְאָתֽוֹ

verses.restored: the soul/life touching it shall be unclean until evening and shall not eat from holy things unless he washes his flesh in water.

familiar.text: The soul which hath touched any such shall be unclean until even, and shall not eat of the holy things, unless he wash his flesh with water.

modern.text: the man who touches any of these will remain unclean until evening. He must not eat from the sacred offerings unless he has bathed himself with water.

original.text: נֶ֚פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּגַּע בּ֔וֹ וְטָמְאָ֖ה עַד הָעָ֑רֶב וְלֹ֤א יֹאכַל֙ מִן הַקֳּדָשִׁ֔ים כִּ֛י אִם רָחַ֥ץ בְּשָׂר֖וֹ בַּמָּֽיִם

verses.restored: When sun goes down, he shall be clean, and afterward he may eat from holy things, for it is his food.

familiar.text: And when the sun is down, he shall be clean, and shall afterward eat of the holy things; because it is his food.

modern.text: When the sun has set, he will become clean, and then he may eat from the sacred offerings, for they are his food.

original.text: וּבָ֥א הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ וְטָהֵ֑ר וְאַחַר֙ יֹאכַ֣ל מִן הַקֳּדָשִׁ֔ים כִּ֥י לַחְמ֖וֹ הֽוּא

verses.restored: Carcass and torn animal he shall not eat to become unclean by it. I am YHWH.

familiar.text: That which dieth of itself, or is torn with beasts, he shall not eat to defile himself therewith: I am the LORD.

modern.text: He must not eat anything found dead or torn by wild animals, which would make him unclean. I am the LORD.

original.text: נְבֵלָ֧ה וּטְרֵפָ֛ה לֹ֥א יֹאכַ֖ל לְטָמְאָה בָ֑הּ אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: They shall keep my charge, lest they bear sin/misalignment because of it and die in it if they profane it. I am YHWH who sanctifies them.

familiar.text: They shall therefore keep mine ordinance, lest they bear sin for it, and die therefore, if they profane it: I the LORD do sanctify them.

modern.text: The priests must keep My charge, lest they bear the guilt and die because they profane it. I am the LORD who sanctifies them.

original.text: וְשָׁמְר֣וּ אֶת מִשְׁמַרְתִּ֗י וְלֹֽא יִשְׂא֤וּ עָלָיו֙ חֵ֔טְא וּמֵ֥תוּ ב֖וֹ כִּ֣י יְחַלְּלֻ֑הוּ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה מְקַדְּשָֽׁם

verses.restored: No stranger shall eat holy thing; resident guest of priest or hired worker shall not eat holy thing.

familiar.text: There shall no stranger eat of the holy thing: a sojourner of the priest, or an hired servant, shall not eat of the holy thing.

modern.text: No one outside a priest’s family may eat the sacred offering, nor may the guest of a priest or his hired hand eat it.

original.text: וְכָל זָ֖ר לֹא יֹ֣אכַל קֹ֑דֶשׁ תּוֹשַׁ֥ב כֹּהֵ֛ן וְשָׂכִ֖יר לֹא יֹ֥אכַל קֹֽדֶשׁ

verses.restored: But when priest buys a soul/life, acquisition of his silver, that one may eat of it, and one born in his house; they may eat from his food.

familiar.text: But if the priest buy any soul with his money, he shall eat of it, and he that is born in his house: they shall eat of his meat.

modern.text: But if a priest buys a slave with his own money, or if a slave is born in his household, that slave may eat his food.

original.text: וְכֹהֵ֗ן כִּֽי יִקְנֶ֥ה נֶ֨פֶשׁ֙ קִנְיַ֣ן כַּסְפּ֔וֹ ה֖וּא יֹ֣אכַל בּ֑וֹ וִילִ֣יד בֵּית֔וֹ הֵ֖ם יֹאכְל֥וּ בְלַחְמֽוֹ

verses.restored: If daughter of priest belongs to a strange man, she shall not eat from contribution of holy things.

familiar.text: If the priest’s daughter also be married unto a stranger, she may not eat of an offering of the holy things.

modern.text: If the priest’s daughter is married to a man other than a priest, she is not to eat of the sacred contributions.

original.text: וּבַת כֹּהֵ֔ן כִּ֥י תִהְיֶ֖ה לְאִ֣ישׁ זָ֑ר הִ֕וא בִּתְרוּמַ֥ת הַקֳּדָשִׁ֖ים לֹ֥א תֹאכֵֽל

verses.restored: But if daughter of priest becomes widow or divorced and has no seed, and returns to house of her father as in her youth, she may eat from food of her father; but no stranger shall eat of it.

familiar.text: But if the priest’s daughter be a widow, or divorced, and have no child, and is returned unto her father’s house, as in her youth, she shall eat of her father’s meat: but there shall no stranger eat thereof.

modern.text: But if a priest’s daughter with no children becomes widowed or divorced and returns to her father’s house, she may share her father’s food as in her youth. But no outsider may share it.

original.text: וּבַת כֹּהֵן֩ כִּ֨י תִהְיֶ֜ה אַלְמָנָ֣ה וּגְרוּשָׁ֗ה וְזֶרַע֮ אֵ֣ין לָהּ֒ וְשָׁבָ֞ה אֶל בֵּ֤ית אָבִ֨יהָ֙ כִּנְעוּרֶ֔יהָ מִלֶּ֥חֶם אָבִ֖יהָ תֹּאכֵ֑ל וְכָל זָ֖ר לֹא יֹ֥אכַל בּֽוֹ

verses.restored: If a man eats holy thing in error/unintentionally, he shall add fifth to it and give holy thing to priest.

familiar.text: And if a man eat of the holy thing unwittingly, then he shall put the fifth part thereof unto it, and shall give it unto the priest with the holy thing.

modern.text: If anyone eats a sacred offering in error, he must add a fifth to its value and give the sacred offering to the priest.

original.text: וְאִ֕ישׁ כִּֽי יֹאכַ֥ל קֹ֖דֶשׁ בִּשְׁגָגָ֑ה וְיָסַ֤ף חֲמִֽשִׁיתוֹ֙ עָלָ֔יו וְנָתַ֥ן לַכֹּהֵ֖ן אֶת הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ

verses.restored: They shall not profane holy things of children of Israel, which they lift to YHWH,

familiar.text: And they shall not profane the holy things of the children of Israel, which they offer unto the LORD;

modern.text: The priests must not profane the sacred offerings that the Israelites present to the LORD

original.text: וְלֹ֣א יְחַלְּל֔וּ אֶת קָדְשֵׁ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר יָרִ֖ימוּ לַיהוָֽה

verses.restored: and so cause them to bear iniquity of guilt/reparation when they eat their holy things; for I am YHWH who sanctifies them.

familiar.text: Or suffer them to bear the iniquity of trespass, when they eat their holy things: for I the LORD do sanctify them.

modern.text: by allowing the people to eat the sacred offerings and thus to bear the punishment for guilt. For I am the LORD who sanctifies them.” Worthy Offerings

verses.restored: Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all children of Israel, and say to them: Any man from house of Israel or from sojourners in Israel who brings near his offering, for any vows or any freewill offerings that they bring near to YHWH for burnt offering,

familiar.text: Speak unto Aaron, and to his sons, and unto all the children of Israel, and say unto them, Whatsoever he be of the house of Israel, or of the strangers in Israel, that will offer his oblation for all his vows, and for all his freewill offerings, which they will offer unto the LORD for a burnt offering;

modern.text: “Speak to Aaron and his sons and all the Israelites and tell them, ‘Any man of the house of Israel or any foreign resident who presents a gift for a burnt offering to the LORD, whether to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering,

original.text: דַּבֵּ֨ר אֶֽל אַהֲרֹ֜ן וְאֶל בָּנָ֗יו וְאֶל֙ כָּל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵהֶ֑ם אִ֣ישׁ אִישׁ֩ מִבֵּ֨ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל וּמִן הַגֵּ֣ר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַקְרִ֤יב קָרְבָּנוֹ֙ לְכָל נִדְרֵיהֶם֙ וּלְכָל נִדְבוֹתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁר יַקְרִ֥יבוּ לַיהוָ֖ה לְעֹלָֽה

verses.restored: for your acceptance it shall be complete male from herd, sheep, or goats.

familiar.text: Ye shall offer at your own will a male without blemish, of the beeves, of the sheep, or of the goats.

modern.text: must offer an unblemished male from the cattle, sheep, or goats in order for it to be accepted on your behalf.

original.text: לִֽרְצֹנְכֶ֑ם תָּמִ֣ים זָכָ֔ר בַּבָּקָ֕ר בַּכְּשָׂבִ֖ים וּבָֽעִזִּֽים

verses.restored: Anything in which there is bodily blemish you shall not bring near, for it shall not be for acceptance for you.

familiar.text: But whatsoever hath a blemish, that shall ye not offer: for it shall not be acceptable for you.

modern.text: You must not present anything with a defect, because it will not be accepted on your behalf.

original.text: כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר בּ֥וֹ מ֖וּם לֹ֣א תַקְרִ֑יבוּ כִּי לֹ֥א לְרָצ֖וֹן יִהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶֽם

verses.restored: When a man brings near sacrifice of peace/well-being offerings to YHWH to fulfill a vow or for freewill offering from herd or flock, it shall be complete for acceptance; no bodily blemish shall be in it.

familiar.text: And whosoever offereth a sacrifice of peace offerings unto the LORD to accomplish his vow, or a freewill offering in beeves or sheep, it shall be perfect to be accepted; there shall be no blemish therein.

modern.text: When a man presents a peace offering to the LORD from the herd or flock to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering, it must be without blemish or defect to be acceptable.

original.text: וְאִ֗ישׁ כִּֽי יַקְרִ֤יב זֶֽבַח שְׁלָמִים֙ לַיהוָ֔ה לְפַלֵּא נֶ֨דֶר֙ א֣וֹ לִנְדָבָ֔ה בַּבָּקָ֖ר א֣וֹ בַצֹּ֑אן תָּמִ֤ים יִֽהְיֶה֙ לְרָצ֔וֹן כָּל מ֖וּם לֹ֥א יִהְיֶה בּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Blind, broken, maimed, having discharge/wart, scab, or skin eruption—you shall not bring these near to YHWH, and fire-offering you shall not give from them on altar to YHWH.

familiar.text: Blind, or broken, or maimed, or having a wen, or scurvy, or scabbed, ye shall not offer these unto the LORD, nor make an offering by fire of them upon the altar unto the LORD.

modern.text: You are not to present to the LORD any animal that is blind, injured, or maimed, or anything with a running sore, a festering rash, or a scab; you must not put any of these on the altar as an offering made by fire to the LORD.

original.text: עַוֶּרֶת֩ א֨וֹ שָׁב֜וּר אוֹ חָר֣וּץ אֽוֹ יַבֶּ֗לֶת א֤וֹ גָרָב֙ א֣וֹ יַלֶּ֔פֶת לֹא תַקְרִ֥יבוּ אֵ֖לֶּה לַיהוָ֑ה וְאִשֶּׁ֗ה לֹא תִתְּנ֥וּ מֵהֶ֛ם עַל הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ לַיהוָֽה

verses.restored: Ox or lamb with limb too long or too short you may make freewill offering, but for vow it shall not be accepted.

familiar.text: Either a bullock or a lamb that hath any thing superfluous or lacking in his parts, that mayest thou offer for a freewill offering; but for a vow it shall not be accepted.

modern.text: You may present as a freewill offering an ox or sheep that has a deformed or stunted limb, but it is not acceptable in fulfillment of a vow.

original.text: וְשׁ֥וֹר וָשֶׂ֖ה שָׂר֣וּעַ וְקָל֑וּט נְדָבָה֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֹת֔וֹ וּלְנֵ֖דֶר לֹ֥א יֵרָצֶֽה

verses.restored: Crushed, bruised, torn, or cut you shall not bring near to YHWH; in your land you shall not do this.

familiar.text: Ye shall not offer unto the LORD that which is bruised, or crushed, or broken, or cut; neither shall ye make any offering thereof in your land.

modern.text: You are not to present to the LORD an animal whose testicles are bruised, crushed, torn, or cut; you are not to sacrifice them in your land.

original.text: וּמָע֤וּךְ וְכָתוּת֙ וְנָת֣וּק וְכָר֔וּת לֹ֥א תַקְרִ֖יבוּ לַֽיהוָ֑ה וּֽבְאַרְצְכֶ֖ם לֹ֥א תַעֲשֽׂוּ

verses.restored: From hand of foreigner you shall not bring bread/food of your Divine from any of these, because their corruption is in them, bodily blemish is in them; they shall not be accepted for you.

familiar.text: Neither from a stranger’s hand shall ye offer the bread of your God of any of these; because their corruption is in them, and blemishes be in them: they shall not be accepted for you.

modern.text: Neither you nor a foreigner shall present food to your God from any such animal. They will not be accepted on your behalf, because they are deformed and flawed.’”

original.text: וּמִיַּ֣ד בֶּן נֵכָ֗ר לֹ֥א תַקְרִ֛יבוּ אֶת לֶ֥חֶם אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֖ם מִכָּל אֵ֑לֶּה כִּ֣י מָשְׁחָתָ֤ם בָּהֶם֙ מ֣וּם בָּ֔ם לֹ֥א יֵרָצ֖וּ לָכֶֽם

verses.restored: When ox or sheep or goat is born, it shall be seven days under its mother, and from eighth day onward it shall be accepted as offering, fire-offering to YHWH.

familiar.text: When a bullock, or a sheep, or a goat, is brought forth, then it shall be seven days under the dam; and from the eighth day and thenceforth it shall be accepted for an offering made by fire unto the LORD.

modern.text: “When an ox, a sheep, or a goat is born, it must remain with its mother for seven days. From the eighth day on, it will be acceptable as an offering made by fire to the LORD.

original.text: שׁ֣וֹר אוֹ כֶ֤שֶׂב אוֹ עֵז֙ כִּ֣י יִוָּלֵ֔ד וְהָיָ֛ה שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים תַּ֣חַת אִמּ֑וֹ וּמִיּ֤וֹם הַשְּׁמִינִי֙ וָהָ֔לְאָה יֵרָצֶ֕ה לְקָרְבַּ֥ן אִשֶּׁ֖ה לַיהוָֽה

verses.restored: Ox or sheep, it and its young you shall not slaughter in one day.

familiar.text: And whether it be cow or ewe, ye shall not kill it and her young both in one day.

modern.text: But you must not slaughter an ox or a sheep on the same day as its young.

original.text: וְשׁ֖וֹר אוֹ שֶׂ֑ה אֹת֣וֹ וְאֶת בְּנ֔וֹ לֹ֥א תִשְׁחֲט֖וּ בְּי֥וֹם אֶחָֽד

verses.restored: When you sacrifice thanksgiving offering to YHWH, for your acceptance you shall sacrifice.

familiar.text: And when ye will offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving unto the LORD, offer it at your own will.

modern.text: When you sacrifice a thank offering to the LORD, offer it so that it may be acceptable on your behalf.

original.text: וְכִֽי תִזְבְּח֥וּ זֶֽבַח תּוֹדָ֖ה לַיהוָ֑ה לִֽרְצֹנְכֶ֖ם תִּזְבָּֽחוּ

verses.restored: On that day it shall be eaten; you shall leave none of it until morning. I am YHWH.

familiar.text: On the same day it shall be eaten up; ye shall leave none of it until the morrow: I am the LORD.

modern.text: It must be eaten that same day. Do not leave any of it until morning. I am the LORD.

original.text: בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ יֵאָכֵ֔ל לֹֽא תוֹתִ֥ירוּ מִמֶּ֖נּוּ עַד בֹּ֑קֶר אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: You shall keep my commandments and do them. I am YHWH.

familiar.text: Therefore shall ye keep my commandments, and do them: I am the LORD.

modern.text: You are to keep My commandments and practice them. I am the LORD.

original.text: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם֙ מִצְוֺתַ֔י וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם אֹתָ֑ם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: You shall not profane my holy name, and I will be sanctified in midst of children of Israel. I am YHWH who sanctifies you,

familiar.text: Neither shall ye profane my holy name; but I will be hallowed among the children of Israel: I am the LORD which hallow you,

modern.text: You must not profane My holy name. I must be acknowledged as holy among the Israelites. I am the LORD who sanctifies you,

translation_notes: Priestly holy-food rules are ritual-boundary rules around food dedicated to YHWH, not human worth ranking.
Temporary impurity resolves by washing and sunset; v.7 confirms return to holy food because it is priestly food.
Household eligibility reflects ancient household economy and requires anti-slavery/gender audit.
Offering blemish restrictions concern ritual acceptability of sacrificial animals, not a theology that disabled bodies are inferior.
Mother-and-young one-day slaughter limit and eighth-day animal rule should be preserved as animal-life boundary.
safety_note: Do not use Leviticus 22 to shame disabled people, illness, poverty, foreigners, women, or household status. The chapter regulates priestly holy food and sacrificial acceptability within an ancient ritual system, while ending with Exodus liberation memory.
